findings.title: Rejected device is cached, so the device limit is bypassed after the first rejection
findings.body: tagDeviceUI sets the local cache entry (line 87) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the device limit is reached, CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, but the cache entry is already set. For the next ~29 minutes, every request from that device hits the cache at line 83 and returns nil, so Authenticate succeeds. Only the first request is rejected. The limit is therefore not enforced consistently, and a new device can authenticate on its second request. The cache should only be set after a successful write, or the entry should be removed on error.

findings.title: Device limit check is a non-atomic count followed by an insert, so concurrent logins can exceed the limit
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first runs CountDevices and only then inserts or updates. Under concurrent anonymous requests from different new devices, several goroutines can read a count below the limit at the same time and all insert, so the number of devices can exceed deviceLimit. Enforcing the limit needs a transactional check-and-insert, or an accepted and documented best-effort tolerance.

findings.title: Device tagging moved into the synchronous auth path, adding a COUNT query and a DB write to every anonymous request
findings.body: The previous implementation tagged devices in a goroutine with a 2-minute timeout and panic recovery. This change calls TagDevice synchronously with the request context. When deviceLimit > 0, every anonymous request that is not served from the local cache now runs a COUNT over anon_device for the last 30 days before the write. Slow DB responses now directly delay or fail the anonymous login path. Consider keeping the work off the request path, or at least documenting the latency impact.

findings.title: No test covers the new Authenticate behaviour when the device limit is reached
findings.body: The new branch in Authenticate that returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, and the change from fire-and-forget to synchronous tagging, are untested. The only new test exercises the store directly (TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit). Nothing checks that Authenticate fails for a rejected device, that a non-limit error is only logged, or that the cache issue above is handled. The existing impl_test tests also do not set a device limit.

findings.title: Frontend type says the device limit may be undefined, but the backend always sends a number
findings.body: anonymousDeviceLimit is typed as `number | undefined`, and GrafanaBootConfig initializes it to undefined. The Go DTO field is a non-pointer int64 with no omitempty, so it is always serialized as a number (0 when unset). The TypeScript type should be `number`, or the field should be made optional on the backend if undefined is intended.

findings.title: New auth.anonymous device_limit option is not documented
findings.body: cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit is read from the new `device_limit` key in [auth.anonymous], but no default or documentation was added to conf/defaults.ini or the docs. The PR's own checklist marks docs as unchecked. Operators have no way to discover the option, and the semantics (0 meaning unlimited, negative values treated as unlimited) are not stated anywhere.
